name: gemm
notes:
One program for every (m, k, n): the shape reaches it only through CRs, and a call
bigger than the tile is that same program launched per tile of an independent dimension. a is
token-major (token i's k elements in rows i*chunks+c), w is output-major (channel j's k weights in
rows j*chunks+c, with one padding row the j loop's last prefetch reads and no multiply ever uses),
b is the n biases in its own region, y is one row per token. chunks = ceil(k/128) and the k chunks
are contracted inside the kernel: per token row R_ACC is zeroed by one word (a's row times the CR
constant 0, ACC.ADD.FIRST), then per chunk and channel one word does MULT.RC.VV of the channel's
128 weights against the token's 128 elements (the lanes past k hold the packer's zeros) and
AGG.SUM, which reduces the products into R_ACC slot j; the next chunk's AGG.SUM adds onto the same
slot, so no partial ever leaves XMEM and no host step joins them. The j loop is software-pipelined:
each word multiplies the row the word before loaded into R_CYCLIC slot 1 (MULT reads it at cycle
start) and advances the pointer by chunks, and the slot counter starts at -1 because AGG reads it
after the word's INC while the branch reads it before. Bias is one word per row: the bias row,
resident in R_CYCLIC slot 2 from a single load, times the CR constant 1.0 with ACC.ADD. The store is
ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE identity with a DS of valid_elements = n, so the n accumulators quantize to the
case's QF with the row's own scale and the lanes past them are written 0. Every instruction is a
hardware one and R_ACC is FP32 in all three variants, so the only rounding is the store's; the
goldens are float64 matmuls of the values XMEM holds and pass with max |err| 0. Domain: m, n from 1
to 128 (one row of R_ACC is one token's 128 outputs) and k from 1 to 2944 = 23 chunks; act takes
only "none" (nothing is fused: an activation is a separate kernel's job) and bias folds b in inside
the kernel. One call must also fit in XMEM, which addresses 16
